at være træt af.explanation: "At være træt af" means "to be tired of". To say something annoys you, put it after "af": "Jeg er træt af regnen" (I am tired of the rain). To say you are sleepy, leave out "af": "Jeg er træt" (I am tired).

at være ude i god tid.explanation: "At være ude i god tid" means "to be well ahead of time". To say you left plenty of time before a flight, say: "Vi er ude i god tid til flyet" (We are in good time for the plane). To say you have plenty of time, use "god tid" (plenty of time) with "have" (have): "Vi har god tid" (We have plenty of time).

at være uenig.explanation: "At være uenig" means "to disagree". To say you disagree with a person, add "med" (with): "Jeg er uenig med dig" (I disagree with you). To name what you disagree about, add "i" (in): "Vi er uenige i det" (We disagree about that).

at være vant til.explanation: "At være vant til" means "to be used to". To say you are used to a thing, put it after "til" (to): "Hun er vant til støjen" (She is used to the noise). To say you are used to doing an action, add "at" (to) and the verb: "Jeg er vant til at stå tidligt op" (I am used to getting up early).

related.en: to be in the habit of

at være ved at.explanation: "At være ved at" means "to be about to / be in the middle of". To say something is about to happen, say: "Toget er ved at køre" (The train is about to leave). To say you are busy doing something right now, say: "Jeg er ved at spise" (I am in the middle of eating).

at være vild med.explanation: "At være vild med" means "to be crazy about". Literally, it is "to be wild with". To say you love a food, put it after "med": "Jeg er vild med pizza" (I love pizza). To say you are crazy about a person, do the same: "Hun er vild med ham" (She is crazy about him).

at være væk.explanation: "At være væk" means "to be gone". To say a person has left, say: "Han er væk" (He is gone). To say a thing has disappeared, say: "Min telefon er væk" (My phone is gone).

at værne om.explanation: "At værne om" means "to protect / safeguard". The small word "om" (about) must always follow "værne". To say what you protect, put it after "om": "Vi skal værne om friheden" (We must protect freedom).

en vaccination.explanation: "En vaccination" means "a vaccination". To say you are going to get the shot, say: "Jeg skal have en vaccination" (I am going to get a vaccination). To talk about the medicine in the shot, use "en vaccine" (a vaccine): "Vaccinen virker" (The vaccine works).

en vaccine.explanation: "En vaccine" means "a vaccine". To say what the vaccine is against, add "mod" (against): "en vaccine mod mæslinger" (a vaccine against measles). To talk about the shot you get at the doctor, use "en vaccination" (a vaccination): "Jeg skal have en vaccination" (I am going to get a vaccination).

en vaffel.explanation: "En vaffel" means "a waffle". It has a second meaning, the crisp cone for ice cream: "Jeg vil gerne have en is i vaffel" (I would like an ice cream in a cone).

en vagt.explanation: "En vagt" means "a guard / shift". When you mean a person who watches a place, it means "a guard": "Vagten står ved porten" (The guard stands at the gate). When you mean a work period, it means "a shift": "Min vagt slutter klokken seks" (My shift ends at six). To say you are on duty, use "at have vagt" (to be on duty) without "en": "Hun har vagt i dag" (She is on duty today).

en vagtlæge.explanation: "En vagtlæge" means "an on-call doctor". It is built from "vagt" (duty) and "læge" (doctor). In Denmark, when your own doctor's office is closed in the evening, at night or at the weekend, you call "lægevagten" (the out-of-hours doctor service) to reach one.

en valgkamp.explanation: "En valgkamp" means "an election campaign". It is built from "valg" (election) and "kamp" (fight), so it is literally a fight for votes. To say the campaign has started, use "i gang" (under way): "Nu er valgkampen i gang" (The election campaign has started).

en valgkreds.explanation: "En valgkreds" means "a constituency". It is built from "valg" (election) and "kreds" (district). To ask which constituency someone lives in, say: "Hvilken valgkreds bor du i?" (Which constituency do you live in?)

en valgmulighed.explanation: "En valgmulighed" means "an option". It is built from "valg" (choice) and "mulighed" (possibility). To say there are several options, use the plural: "Der er flere valgmuligheder" (There are several options).

related.en: something you choose to leave out

en valnød.explanation: "En valnød" means "a walnut". The last part, "nød" (nut), is also in "en jordnød" (a peanut).

en valuta.explanation: "En valuta" means "a currency". To talk about money from another country, add "udenlandsk" (foreign): "udenlandsk valuta" (foreign currency).

en vampyr.explanation: "En vampyr" means "a vampire". Danish spells it with a "y" in the last part, where English has an "i".

en vandflaske.explanation: "En vandflaske" means "a water bottle". It is built from "vand" (water) and "flaske" (bottle).

en vandhane.explanation: "En vandhane" means "a faucet / tap". It is built from "vand" (water) and "hane", which means "rooster" and also "tap". To tell someone to turn off the tap, say: "Luk for vandhanen" (Turn off the faucet).

en vandkande.explanation: "En vandkande" means "a watering can". It is built from "vand" (water) and "kande" (jug), the same "kande" as in "en kaffekande" (a coffee pot).

en vandkaraffel.explanation: "En vandkaraffel" means "a water carafe". It is built from "vand" (water) and "karaffel" (carafe).

en vandmand.explanation: "En vandmand" means "a jellyfish". It is built from "vand" (water) and "mand" (man). The plural is "vandmænd", with "æ" instead of "a".

en vandmelon.explanation: "En vandmelon" means "a watermelon". It is built from "vand" (water) and "melon" (melon). To ask for a piece, say: "en skive vandmelon" (a slice of watermelon).

en vandpyt.explanation: "En vandpyt" means "a puddle". It is built from "vand" (water) and "pyt" (puddle). The word "pyt" is also what Danes say to let something go: "Pyt!" (Never mind!)

en vandregning.explanation: "En vandregning" means "a water bill". It is built from "vand" (water) and "regning" (bill). In a restaurant, "regning" also means the check: "Regningen, tak" (The check, please).

en vandretur.explanation: "En vandretur" means "a hike". It is built from "at vandre" (to hike) and "tur" (trip), the same "tur" as in "en cykeltur" (a bike ride).

en vane.explanation: "En vane" means "a habit". To say you have a habit of doing something, use "at have for vane" (to be in the habit of) with "at" and a verb: "Jeg har for vane at gå en tur" (I am in the habit of going for a walk).

en vaniljekrans.explanation: "En vaniljekrans" means "a vanilla butter cookie". It is a traditional Danish Christmas cookie. It is built from "vanilje" (vanilla) and "krans" (wreath).

en vanskelighed.explanation: "En vanskelighed" means "a difficulty". It comes from the adjective "vanskelig" (difficult). To say someone has difficulty doing something, use the plural with "med" (with): "Hun har vanskeligheder med at høre" (She has difficulty hearing).

en vante.explanation: "En vante" means "a mitten". A glove with a space for each finger is "en handske" (a glove): "Jeg har røde handsker på" (I am wearing red gloves).

en vare.explanation: "En vare" means "an item / product". To talk about goods in a shop, use the plural "varer" (goods): "Butikken har mange varer" (The shop has many goods). For a thing you own, use "en ting" (a thing): "Jeg har mange ting i skabet" (I have many things in the closet).

en varedeklaration.explanation: "En varedeklaration" means "a product label". It is built from "vare" (product) and "deklaration" (declaration). To tell someone to check what is in the food, say: "Læs varedeklarationen" (Read the product label).

en vareprøve.explanation: "En vareprøve" means "a product sample". To say the sample costs nothing, add "gratis" (free): "en gratis vareprøve" (a free product sample).

en varevogn.explanation: "En varevogn" means "a van". It is built from "varer" (goods) and "vogn" (wagon), the same "vogn" as in "en indkøbsvogn" (a shopping cart).

en variation.explanation: "En variation" means "a variation". To say what the variation is based on, add "over" (on): "en variation over en gammel opskrift" (a variation on an old recipe).

en varmebølge.explanation: "En varmebølge" means "a heat wave". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "bølge" (wave). To say a heat wave is on its way, say: "Der kommer en varmebølge" (A heat wave is coming).

en varmepumpe.explanation: "En varmepumpe" means "a heat pump". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "pumpe" (pump).

en varmerekord.explanation: "En varmerekord" means "a record high temperature". It is built from "varme" (heat) and "rekord" (record). To talk about the opposite, use "en kulderekord" (a record low): "Der blev sat en kulderekord i går" (A record low was set yesterday).

en vase.explanation: "En vase" means "a vase". To say what is in it, add "med" (with): "en vase med roser" (a vase with roses).

en vask.explanation: "En vask" means "a sink". It comes from the verb "at vaske" (to wash). To say you wash your hands, use the verb: "Jeg vasker mine hænder" (I wash my hands).

en vaskekælder.explanation: "En vaskekælder" means "a laundry room". It is built from "vaske" (to wash) and "kælder" (basement). In Denmark, an apartment building can have one that all the residents share.

en vaskemaskine.explanation: "En vaskemaskine" means "a washing machine". It is built from "at vaske" (to wash) and "en maskine" (a machine). To say you start it, use "sætte i gang" (to get going): "Jeg sætter vaskemaskinen i gang" (I start the washing machine).

en vatpind.explanation: "En vatpind" means "a cotton swab". It is built from "vat" (cotton wool) and "pind" (stick), the same "pind" as in "en spisepind" (a chopstick).

en vedhæftet fil.explanation: "En vedhæftet fil" means "an attachment". Literally, it is "an attached file". To tell someone to look at the attachment in an email, write: "Se den vedhæftede fil" (See the attached file).

en veganer.explanation: "En veganer" means "a vegan". Do not mix it up with "en vegetar" (a vegetarian): "Han er vegetar og spiser æg" (He is a vegetarian and eats eggs).

en vegetar.explanation: "En vegetar" means "a vegetarian". To describe food, use "vegetarisk" (vegetarian): "en vegetarisk ret" (a vegetarian dish).

en vej.explanation: "En vej" means "a road". It has a second meaning, "a way" or route: "Hvilken vej skal jeg gå?" (Which way should I go?). To ask for directions, say "at spørge om vej" (to ask for directions), with no "en" before "vej": "Jeg vil spørge om vej" (I will ask for directions).

en vejleder.explanation: "En vejleder" means "a supervisor". It comes from the verb "at vejlede" (to guide).

en vejledning.explanation: "En vejledning" means "a guide". It is the noun for the verb "at vejlede" (to guide). To say what the guide is for, add "til" (for): "en vejledning til programmet" (a guide for the program).

en vejrmelding.explanation: "En vejrmelding" means "a weather report". It is built from "vejr" (weather) and "melding" (message), the same "melding" as in "en fejlmelding" (an error message).

en vejrudsigt.explanation: "En vejrudsigt" means "a weather forecast". It is built from "vejr" (weather) and "udsigt" (outlook). "Udsigt" also means "a view" by itself: "Der er en flot udsigt" (There is a great view).

en vejviser.explanation: "En vejviser" means "a signpost". It is built from "vej" (road) and "viser" (pointer, from "at vise", to show). It has a second meaning, a printed directory of addresses: "Jeg slog adressen op i vejviseren" (I looked up the address in the directory).

en vekselkurs.explanation: "En vekselkurs" means "an exchange rate". It is built from "at veksle" (to exchange) and "kurs" (rate).

en velsignelse.explanation: "En velsignelse" means "a blessing". It also means something that is a great help: "Din hjælp er en velsignelse" (Your help is a blessing).

en ven.explanation: "En ven" means "a friend". It is the word for a friend of either sex: "Hun er min bedste ven" (She is my best friend). Do not mix it up with "en kæreste" (boyfriend or girlfriend): "Han er min kæreste" (He is my boyfriend).

en veninde.explanation: "En veninde" means "a female friend". To say a male friend, use "en ven" (a friend): "Han er min ven" (He is my friend).

en vennegruppe.explanation: "En vennegruppe" means "a group of friends". It is built from "venner" (friends) and "gruppe" (group), the same "gruppe" as in "en studiegruppe" (a study group).

en venteliste.explanation: "En venteliste" means "a waiting list". To say you are on a waiting list, use "stå på venteliste" (to be on a waiting list) without "en": "Hun står på venteliste til en lejlighed" (She is on the waiting list for an apartment).

en ventetid.explanation: "En ventetid" means "a wait time". It is built from "at vente" (to wait) and "en tid" (a time). To ask how long you will wait, say: "Hvor lang er ventetiden?" (How long is the wait?)

en ventilator.explanation: "En ventilator" means "a fan", as in the machine that moves air. A fan of a team is "en fan" (a fan): "Jeg er fan af holdet" (I am a fan of the team).

en verden.explanation: "En verden" means "a world". To say something happens everywhere, use "i hele verden" (all over the world): "Man spiller fodbold i hele verden" (People play soccer all over the world). To say something is the best in the world, add "s" to "verden": "Det er verdens bedste kage" (It is the best cake in the world).

en verdensdel.explanation: "En verdensdel" means "a continent". It is built from "verden" (world) and "del" (part), so it is literally "world part".

en verdenskrig.explanation: "En verdenskrig" means "a world war". It is built from "verden" (world) and "krig" (war). To name the two world wars, say "første verdenskrig" (the First World War) and "anden verdenskrig" (the Second World War).

en version.explanation: "En version" means "a version". To talk about a new release, say: "den nye version af appen" (the new version of the app). To talk about one person's account of what happened, say: "Hun fortalte sin version" (She told her version).

en vest.explanation: "En vest" means "a vest", as in the sleeveless garment worn over a shirt. The word is also in "en redningsvest" (a life jacket): "Børnene har redningsveste på" (The children are wearing life jackets).

en veteran.explanation: "En veteran" means "a veteran". It also means a very experienced person: "Hun er en veteran i branchen" (She is a veteran in the industry). As the first part of a compound, it means old but well kept: "en veteranbil" (a vintage car).

en vicepræsident.explanation: "En vicepræsident" means "a vice president". It is built from "vice" (deputy) and "præsident" (president). Denmark has a monarch, not a president. To talk about the vice president of the USA, say: "USA's vicepræsident" (the vice president of the USA).

en vicevært.explanation: "En vicevært" means "a caretaker / janitor". It is built from "vice" (deputy) and "vært" (host), so it is literally a deputy host.

en videnskab.explanation: "En videnskab" means "a science". To name the school subject science, use "naturfag" (natural science subjects): "Vi har naturfag i dag" (We have science today).

en videnskabsmand.explanation: "En videnskabsmand" means "a scientist". It is built from "videnskab" (science) and "mand" (man), a pattern also used in "en brandmand" (a firefighter).

en video.explanation: "En video" means "a video". To say you record a video, use "at optage" (to record): "Jeg optager en video" (I record a video).

en vielsesring.explanation: "En vielsesring" means "a wedding ring". It is built from "vielse" (wedding ceremony) and "ring" (ring). Do not mix it up with "en forlovelsesring" (an engagement ring): "Hun fik en forlovelsesring i går" (She got an engagement ring yesterday).

en vikar.explanation: "En vikar" means "a substitute teacher". To say a temp in another job, add the place: "en vikar på kontoret" (a temp at the office).

en viking.explanation: "En viking" means "a Viking". To talk about a Viking ship, use "et vikingeskib" (a Viking ship): "Vi så et vikingeskib på museet" (We saw a Viking ship at the museum).

en vilje.explanation: "En vilje" means "a will", as in willpower. To say you did something on purpose, use "med vilje" (on purpose), without "en": "Han gjorde det med vilje" (He did it on purpose).

en villa.explanation: "En villa" means "a detached house". Unlike the English word "villa", it does not have to be fancy: in Denmark it is an ordinary family house.

en vin.explanation: "En vin" means "a wine". To name the color of the wine, join it to "vin": "en rødvin" (a red wine) or "en hvidvin" (a white wine). To order a drink, say: "et glas vin" (a glass of wine).

en vinbar.explanation: "En vinbar" means "a wine bar". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "bar" (bar).

en vinder.explanation: "En vinder" means "a winner". It comes from the verb "at vinde" (to win). The opposite is "en taber" (a loser): "Han er en dårlig taber" (He is a bad loser).

en vindmølle.explanation: "En vindmølle" means "a wind turbine / windmill". It is built from "vind" (wind) and "mølle" (mill).

en vindrue.explanation: "En vindrue" means "a grape". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "drue" (grape). To talk about a bunch of grapes, say: "en klase vindruer" (a bunch of grapes).

en vindueskarm.explanation: "En vindueskarm" means "a windowsill". To say something sits on the windowsill, Danish uses "i" (in) where English uses "on": "Katten sidder i vindueskarmen" (The cat sits on the windowsill).

en vinduesplads.explanation: "En vinduesplads" means "a window seat". The opposite is "en gangplads" (an aisle seat): "Jeg vil gerne have en gangplads" (I would like an aisle seat).

en vinduespudsning.explanation: "En vinduespudsning" means "a window cleaning". It comes from "at pudse" (to polish). To say you shine your shoes, use the same verb: "Jeg pudser mine sko" (I polish my shoes).

en vinduesvisker.explanation: "En vinduesvisker" means "a windshield wiper". It is built from "vindue" (window) and "visker" (wiper).

en vinge.explanation: "En vinge" means "a wing", as in the wing of a bird or a plane. For the wing of a building, use "en fløj" (a wing): "Slottet har to fløje" (The castle has two wings).

en vinhandel.explanation: "En vinhandel" means "a wine shop". The word "handel" (trade) is also in "en blomsterhandel" (a flower shop).

en vinkel.explanation: "En vinkel" means "an angle". In math, it is the angle between two lines: "en ret vinkel" (a right angle). To talk about a way of looking at something, say: "Jeg ser det fra en anden vinkel" (I see it from another angle).

en vinliste.explanation: "En vinliste" means "a wine list". It is built from "vin" (wine) and "liste" (list), the same "liste" as in "en gæsteliste" (a guest list). To ask the waiter for it, say: "Må jeg se vinlisten?" (May I see the wine list?)

en vinter.explanation: "En vinter" means "a winter". To say what happens every winter, use "om vinteren" (in the winter): "Om vinteren er det koldt" (In the winter it is cold).

en vinterbader.explanation: "En vinterbader" means "a winter swimmer". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "at bade" (to swim). "At bade" means going into the sea or a lake for fun: "Vi bader i søen" (We swim in the lake).

en vinterdag.explanation: "En vinterdag" means "a winter day". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "dag" (day), and the same "vinter" is in "en vinterferie" (a winter break).

en vinterferie.explanation: "En vinterferie" means "a winter break". In Denmark, school children have it in February.

en vinterjakke.explanation: "En vinterjakke" means "a winter jacket". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "jakke" (jacket), the same "jakke" as in "en læderjakke" (a leather jacket).

en vinternat.explanation: "En vinternat" means "a winter night". It is built from "vinter" (winter) and "nat" (night). To say you slept badly last night, use "i nat" (last night): "Jeg sov dårligt i nat" (I slept badly last night).

en vinterstøvle.explanation: "En vinterstøvle" means "a winter boot". To talk about more than one boot, use the plural: "Jeg tager vinterstøvler på" (I put on winter boots).

en violin.explanation: "En violin" means "a violin". Danish has a second word, "en fiol" (a fiddle): "Han spiller fiol til dans" (He plays fiddle for dancing).

en vippe.explanation: "En vippe" means "a seesaw". The same word is in "en øjenvippe" (an eyelash): "Hun har lange øjenvipper" (She has long eyelashes).
